nodes.title: Size of the Perrin numbers at negative indices

nodes.summary: Write $R_n$ for the Perrin sequence and $R_{-n}$ for its extension to negative indices, for natural numbers $n$. The two definitions give the same value at index $0$, and the Perrin recurrence holds across index $0$: $R_2 = R_0 + R_{-1}$ and $R_1 = R_{-1} + R_{-2}$.
nodes.title: The Perrin sequence and its backward extension fit together at index zero

nodes.summary: Let $R_{-k}$ denote the Perrin sequence extended to negative indices. The pairs of positive integers $(n, m)$ with $R_{-n} = R_{-m}^2$ or $R_{-n} = -R_{-m}^2$ are exactly the pairs with $n, m \in \{1, 2, 7, 11, 29\}$, together with $(5, 3)$, $(5, 6)$, $(5, 20)$, $(18, 8)$ and $(18, 16)$.
nodes.title: Negative-index Perrin numbers equal to plus or minus a negative-index Perrin square

nodes.summary: Let $R_k$ denote the Perrin sequence, extended to negative indices. The pairs of positive integers $(n, m)$ with $R_{-n} = R_m^2$ or $R_{-n} = -R_m^2$ are exactly $(5, 2)$, $(5, 4)$, $(18, 5)$ and $(18, 6)$; that is, $R_{-5} = 4 = R_2^2 = R_4^2$ and $R_{-18} = 25 = R_5^2 = R_6^2$.
nodes.title: Negative-index Perrin numbers equal to plus or minus a Perrin square

nodes.summary: Let $R_{-k}$ denote the Perrin sequence extended to negative indices. For every natural number $n$, $R_{-n} = R_{-(n+2)} + R_{-(n+3)}$.
nodes.title: Perrin recurrence at negative indices

nodes.summary: The Perrin sequence $R_k$ extended to negative indices satisfies $R_{-5} = 4$, $R_{-18} = 25$, $R_{-1} = R_{-7} = R_{-11} = R_{-29} = -1$ and $R_{-2} = 1$.
nodes.title: Some values of the Perrin sequence at negative indices

nodes.summary: The Perrin sequence $R_k$, given by $R_0 = 3$, $R_1 = 0$, $R_2 = 2$ and $R_{k+3} = R_{k+1} + R_k$, extends uniquely to all integers $k$ by running the recurrence backward. This defines the integers $R_{-n}$ for natural numbers $n$: $R_0 = 3$, $R_{-1} = -1$, $R_{-2} = 1$ and $R_{-(n+3)} = R_{-n} - R_{-(n+2)}$ for every $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Perrin sequence at negative indices

nodes.summary: Let $R_n$ denote the $n$-th term of the Perrin sequence. For positive integers $n$ and $m$, $R_n = R_m^2$ holds if and only if $n = m = 1$ (where $R_1 = 0 = R_1^2$).
nodes.title: Perrin numbers that are squares of Perrin numbers

nodes.summary: Let $R_n$ denote the $n$-th term of the Perrin sequence and $R_{-m}$ the term at index $-m$ of its backward extension to negative indices. For all positive integers $n$ and $m$, $R_n \ne R_{-m}^2$.
nodes.title: No positive-index Perrin number is the square of a negative-index one

nodes.summary: Let $R_n$ denote the $n$-th term of the Perrin sequence and $R_{-n}$ the term at index $-n$ of its backward extension to negative indices. For every natural number $n$, $R_n = 0$ if and only if $n = 1$, and $R_{-n} \ne 0$. Thus $R_1 = 0$ is the only zero of the sequence $(R_k)_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$.
nodes.title: The only zero of the two-sided Perrin sequence
